args: 2_what we do in the shadows is a bracing reminder of how the right burst of energy and style breathes fresh ideas into a genre threatened with creative exhaustion.
6_"what we do in the shadows" is bloody awesome.
7_there is so much love and understanding of all the genres the film is skewering that "what we do in the shadows" transcends its lowbrow inspirations.
16_"what we do in the shadows" is an irrepressibly charming b-movie that never over-stays its welcome, and is both conceptually clever and admirably well-executed.
17_like a christopher guest movie with a widow's peak, what we do in the shadows depicts a supposed "new zealand documentary board" film gone gruesomely, hilariously awry.
18_just when it looked like the vampire genre had been bled dry, along comes the insanely inspired horror-satire "what we do in the shadows" to give it fresh bite.
20_what we do in the shadows leaps to the top of the pack, by resolutely sticking to deadpan humour and absurd riffs on the awkwardness of being a vampire in a world made for humans.
24_is this new zealand mockumentary just one comedy sketch stretched to movie length?
25_most of the best gags are in the early going and the film seems ever more stretched and thin as it goes on.
28_what we do in the shadows is never as self-conscious as you fear it might be, and it has some of the loose, wiggy energy of early jim jarmusch, only with more bite.
29_i found myself cackling at "what we do in the shadows" like a witch with a helium balloon.

9_it's a cheerfully horrific affair, a sanguine comedy that feels more than a bit like a christopher guest farce or an elaborate monty python sketch, imprinted with the kiwi comic sensibilities of co-directors jemaine clement and taika waititi.
13_you've got to love a thing to skewer it as thoroughly as taika waititi and jemaine clement do in their delightfully silly vampire mockumentary "what we do in the shadows."
